title: Claude Code: 2026 Agentic Features
content:
## Overview

Since mid-2025, Claude Code has moved from a single-agent terminal assistant toward a layered agentic system: memory, hooks, skills, subagents, plugins, and MCP are now distinct, composable layers. This page tracks the features that made that shift, most of which landed between late 2025 and mid-2026.

---

## Plugins & Marketplaces

Claude Code plugins launched **October 9, 2025**. A plugin bundles any combination of:

- **Skills** — instruction sets for handling specific task types
- **Agents** — specialized subagents for particular workflows
- **Hooks** — scripts that run at defined lifecycle points
- **MCP servers** — pre-configured connections to external services

Plugins are distributed through **marketplaces** — a GitHub repository with a `marketplace.json` registry that Claude Code reads to discover installable plugins. Each plugin lives in its own subdirectory with a `plugin.json` manifest describing it.

- `claude-plugins-official` is added automatically to every install.
- `anthropics/claude-plugins-community` must be added manually; it only carries plugins that passed automated safety screening.
- Teams can also stand up a private marketplace repo for internal-only plugins.

---

## Auto Mode

Auto Mode replaces per-action permission prompts with a background safety classifier, letting Claude Code run longer stretches of work without interruption:

- Originally Opus-only, Auto Mode now also runs on **Sonnet 4.6** and is available on **Pro accounts**, not just Max.
- Every action is routed through a Sonnet 4.6 safety classifier before execution.
- Available on third-party hosting as well: Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry, for Opus 4.7 and Opus 4.8.

---

## Nested Subagents

Subagent spawning is now **hierarchical**: a parent agent can create child agents up to **three levels deep**. This enables layered task decomposition — a top-level coordinator delegates to mid-level subagents, which in turn delegate narrower pieces of work to their own subagents, useful for operations spanning many modules or files at once.

Related reliability features introduced alongside deeper nesting:

- **Fallback model chains** — if a subagent's primary model is unavailable or rate-limited, it automatically retries on a configured fallback model.
- **Per-agent cost attribution** — token/cost usage is tracked per subagent, not just per session, making it possible to see which branch of a multi-agent task is expensive.
- **Scoped permissions** — each subagent can be restricted to a subset of tools/permissions rather than inheriting the parent's full access.

---

## Routines & Scheduled/Remote Tasks

"Routines" extend Claude Code's scheduled-task model: set up a prompt once, connect the tools it needs, and pick when it runs.

- **Remote routines** run entirely on Anthropic's cloud infrastructure — they do not require a laptop or local session to stay open.
- Routines can be driven and monitored from **mobile and web surfaces**, not just the CLI.
- Claude Code can send **push notifications** when a routine or long-running task finishes, so users don't have to poll a session for completion.

This wiki's own maintenance agent (see `wikis/AGENT_PROMPT.md`) is an example of a routine: a stored prompt that runs on a schedule with full read/write access to the repo.

---

## Other Notable Additions

- **Ultrathink / `/ultrareview`** — deeper, more deliberate reasoning modes for complex review or planning tasks, distinct from the default reasoning depth.
- **GitHub-loaded skills for Managed Agents** — skills can now be pulled directly from a GitHub repo for use in server-hosted Managed Agents sessions, rather than bundled locally.
- **Budget caps, advisor support, and geo control** were added to the Claude Developer Platform for Managed Agents sessions, giving teams cost ceilings and regional routing for hosted agent workloads.

---

## Why This Matters

The common thread across these features is separating **what an agent can do** (skills, MCP servers) from **how much autonomy it has** (Auto Mode, scoped permissions) from **when and where it runs** (routines, remote/mobile, Managed Agents). Earlier Claude Code was essentially one agent in one terminal session; by mid-2026 it's a set of composable primitives for building fleets of agents with different trust levels, schedules, and cost budgets.
